- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". content.text:
h15.

Memo view-visibility is enforced at several independent server surfaces (all keyed off `store.Memo.Visibility` = Public/Protected/Private plus creator/role checks):

Single-memo read gate (`checkMemoReadAccess`, used by GetMemo / ListMemoComments) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-68 (called at memo_service.go:356, 367 and memo_service_comments.go:148)
List-query visibility scoping (`ListMemos` builds `VisibilityList`/creator filter) — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:218-227
Attachment/file access gate (`checkAttachmentPermission`, resolves the linked memo's visibility) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:649-704
RSS feed (restricts feed items to `store.Public`) — server/router/rss/rss.go:90, 141
Sitemap XML (lists only `store.Public` memos) — server/router/frontend/frontend.go:149-151

The first three are the substantive "who may view this memo" gates; the RSS and sitemap surfaces enforce the same rule by hard-limiting their queries to public memos. (Note: the comment-create check at memo_service.go / memo_service_comments.go:41 and the share-management checks in memo_share_service.go are write/ownership gates, not view gates.)
